cards.title: Pack the medicines before the sarees
cards.body: Clothes can be bought anywhere. That one BP tablet in a small town on a Sunday, maybe not. Here's the list.

cards.title: Enough for the trip, plus extra
cards.body: Carry the full supply for the trip and a few extra days in case of delays. Your chemist can help you work out the quantity.

cards.title: Hand luggage, always
cards.body: Medicines go in the bag that stays with your parent, not the suitcase under the train berth or in the plane's hold.

cards.title: Original strips and the prescription
cards.body: Keep medicines in labelled strips and carry the latest prescription, on paper and as a photo. Useful if you need a chemist on the way.

cards.title: Timings on the move
cards.body: Overnight trains and flights mess with routines. Ask the doctor or pharmacist how to time doses while travelling, especially diabetes medicines.

cards.title: The small extras
cards.body: Water, a snack if they're on sugar medicines, any BP or sugar meter they use, and emergency contacts written on paper.

cards.title: Pack it first, then relax
cards.body: Medicine pouch packed first, checked twice, kept close. Then go enjoy the trip.

takeaway: Carry enough medicines plus extra, in original strips, in hand luggage, with the prescription and a timing plan from the doctor.
share: Forward this before the next family shaadi trip.
